dedupe_keys.name: common ground alliance dirt underground facility damage reports and dashboard

description: The Damage Information Reporting Tool (DIRT) of the Common Ground Alliance collects reports of damage to buried utilities in the United States and Canada, submitted voluntarily by facility operators, locating companies, 811 one-call centres, contractors and regulators. Each year the CGA publishes a DIRT report analysing the data by facility type, excavation work, root cause and region. Telecommunications is the most damaged buried infrastructure: in 2019 nearly 205,000 underground telecom facilities were damaged, more than gas, electric and water combined, and in 2025, out of 221,717 unique damage reports, telecom and cable (MSO/CATV) lines accounted for 51 per cent, with 70 per cent of those caused by other utilities' work. The top causes include failing to call 811 before digging, not keeping clearance after marking and inaccurate marking by locators. Since 2023 the CGA has published a CGA Index comparing years against a 2022 baseline, which stood at 102 in 2025, and an interactive Damage Prevention Dashboard combining 811 centre and DIRT data for 2023 to 2025. Coverage: the United States and Canada, annual. Format and access: annual report PDF and online dashboard, free; the underlying records are not released. Caveats: voluntary and duplicated reporting, so counts are modelled; causes are reported by submitters. Simulation uses: failure rates and causes for buried fibre and cable, repair and restoration planning, and interdependency with other utilities' works. Related records: FCC NORS outage reports include fibre cuts as a cause.
